chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Beginning to try to get work in 1934 with help from uncle Harry
summary: Harry introduced her to musicians and looked for openings, humiliating at first.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: That was about it. I didn't have alot of those earlier experiences. Once I got that opportunity to sing alone with Harry, and I was quite sheltered, you know. In fact this Club, this Club in Stuenville, Ohio where I worked with Harry, they served three-point-two beers, you know. I think they probably served a little bit of wine. But anyway, I could have the three-and-two-tenths percent beer, but the management told the boys that if he caught any of them giving me anything stronger that they would be fired. So that was my first taste of the night club business, you know.

Now I wasn't a baby, you know, but I think because I was small everybody must have considered I was much younger than I was. But I certainly wasn't a minor. I was old enough. They just didn't want to believe it.
Okay, and that's when things started to happen for you?
That's when I figured - and Harry might have had a lot to do with that, you know.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

I mean introduce me to other musicians and trying to find an opening for me somewhere. But I couldn't get into the local clubs. My voice wasn't strong enough. I was certainly not experienced enough. I had a pretty rough time. Even when I finally got that job at the B.H.L. Club I wasn't sure that I was going to make it because they had another singer there, and the experience that you had to have, you had to be very sophisticated and take money off the tables, if you know what I mean. They had a table until somebody went in their pocket and gave you a tip. And that, sort of, bothered me a little bit. I was a little shy. I wanted to just sing and get back to the piano.
Yes, it was a little bit for me. And those were some of the things that held me back. Some things that I just couldn't get it into my system to do.
